sections.h2: How do you file a deed with the Hillsdale County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
You can file in person at the County Office Building, 33 McCollum St., Room 212, Hillsdale 49242, or call (517) 437-2231. The counter keeps weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Electronic submissions may arrive at any hour, though staff process them only when the office is open and skip holidays.

Four e-recording vendors are approved: Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile and CSC/Ingeo. They are paid by ACH, may add charges of their own, and return the recorded document electronically. The register may reject any electronic filing that breaks the Michigan Recording Act.

Paper filings cannot be paid with a personal check. Certified funds, such as a cashier's check or money order, work. The office will not draft documents, hand over templates, or offer anything that sounds like legal advice, and its web page lists three Hillsdale title companies for owners who want help.

sections.h2: What does Hillsdale County charge for recording?
sections.html:
The base price is $30.00 for a whole document, under MCL 600.2567 as amended by PA 224 of 2016. Smaller items are in the county's schedule.

Hillsdale County register of deeds price schedule
ItemAmount
Recording a document, any length$30.00
Each further assignment or discharge$3.00
Tax certificate covering five descriptions$5.00
Search by grantor or grantee$5.00 minimum, 50 cents for each year searched
Plain copy of a real estate record$1.00 per page
Certification of a copy$5.00 per document

Searches for state or federal tax liens are $3.00 a name, and plat copies are $2.00 a page. The register's page includes a calculator for transfer tax, and staff finalize the amount when the deed is presented.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies to a Hillsdale County sale?
sections.html:
Round the price up to the next $500, then multiply the count of $500 blocks by $4.30. That figure joins 55 cents for the county (MCL 207.504) with $3.75 for the state (MCL 207.525).

A $175,000 sale has 350 blocks. The state gets $1,312.50, the county $192.50, and the total is $1,505.00. For the median owner-occupied value of $176,100 the base moves to $176,500, so 353 blocks and $1,517.90.

  • Print the full price on the deed or file a value affidavit.
  • Write any exemption on the instrument itself.
  • County exemptions sit in MCL 207.505 and state ones in MCL 207.526.
  • A land contract is exempt until legal title passes, and the later deed has to cite the contract.

sections.h2: Which 2018 law changes still matter for a Hillsdale County deed?
sections.html:
On June 22, 2018 the register told title companies, attorneys and lenders about Public Acts 191 to 200, signed two days earlier. The pieces affecting most deeds took effect on September 19, 2018.

  • Survivor language needs proof of death. A certified death certificate must be recorded by liber and page, or filed with the deed as its own document. A copy stapled to the deed no longer satisfies MCL 565.48.
  • A document signed elsewhere must follow Michigan recording rules, apart from page layout (MCL 565.203).
  • Text in another language needs an English translation attached (MCL 565.201).

The office adds that court orders must carry the clerk's certification and seal, acknowledgment dates cannot be blank, and fees are collected the moment a document is presented.

sections.h2: What does the Hillsdale register check on every deed?
sections.html:
The office publishes a checklist drawn from Michigan statutes, and a deed that misses a line can be turned away at the counter.

  • Original signatures with names typed or printed beneath, matching the names in the notary's acknowledgment (MCL 565.201).
  • The grantee's street or post office address and the name and business address of the drafter.
  • An acknowledgment by a judge, court clerk or notary in Michigan for any document signed in the state.
  • Black ink, 10 point type, white 20 pound paper, a 2.5 inch top margin on page one and half inch margins elsewhere, with one statement naming the recordable event.
  • Total value on the face of the deed, or a value affidavit attached.
  • No more than the last four digits of a Social Security number.
  • A certificate of trust, where a trust is involved, that follows MCL 565.432 and 565.433.

Before April 6, 2017, a deed also had to say whether male grantors were married or single. That rule applies only to deeds signed before that date.

sections.h2: How do you search Hillsdale County deed records?
sections.html:
The register's page offers search by full text, using optical character recognition, and by name, date, and liber and page. Tract books are linked through Kofile. An owner who wants a deed corrected should know that the office cannot change or alter a document already recorded or in the middle of recording.

Title companies do much of the research for a sale. The register's page names three in the city of Hillsdale: Public Title, Midstate Title and Bell Title Tri County. Ask whichever one handles your closing to confirm the transfer tax figure, since the register collects it with the recording fee.

sections.h2: What does the Hillsdale County Treasurer require before and after a closing?
sections.html:
A warranty deed, a land contract, or an assignment of one with a warranty clause needs the Treasurer's certificate under MCL 211.135. It costs $5.00 for up to five descriptions, and the Treasurer's line is (517) 437-4700.

The Treasurer's delinquent tax notice explains the final stretch of the foreclosure law. A cutoff date decides whose names run in a newspaper ad for two weeks ahead of the Show Cause Hearing in Circuit Court. Shortly afterward the office quits taking partial payments and personal or business checks, and accepts only cash, cashier's checks, money orders and credit cards, which carry a 3% convenience fee. The notice urges owners to pay rather than risk a valuable property.

An owner with an old balance should get a payoff figure before listing, since the deed waits on the certificate.

The Territorial legislature described the county in 1829 and it was organized in 1835, named for its rolling land. Hillsdale is the seat and the largest city, and Hillsdale College is there. At 607 square miles, the county is the only one in Michigan bordering both Indiana and Ohio, and it holds Michigan's southernmost point. Two separate St. Joseph Rivers begin here, one flowing toward Lake Michigan and one toward the Maumee. McCourtie Park and Slayton Arboretum are local parks. Jackson, Calhoun, Lenawee and Branch counties border it in Michigan, with Fulton and Williams counties in Ohio and Steuben County in Indiana to the south.

The average July high is 82 degrees, January's is 29, and June is the wettest month at about 4.3 inches.

The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 45,738 residents, about level with the 45,746 of 2020 and under the 46,688 of 2010. For 2020 to 2024 it reports 17,860 households, a median owner-occupied value of $176,100, 82.0% owner occupancy, median household income of $64,242, median rent of $832, and 23.2% of residents at 65 or older. With owners in four of every five homes, most deeds recorded here are home sales.

The register also offers a free Property Alert service that warns landowners of possible property fraud.

faqs.q: What is the Hillsdale County fee to record a deed?
faqs.a: $30.00 for the document, however long it is. A sale adds transfer tax, and a warranty deed needs a $5.00 treasurer's certificate.

faqs.q: Can a Hillsdale County deed be recorded electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile and CSC/Ingeo are approved vendors, paid by ACH, and they may charge fees of their own.

faqs.q: Does Hillsdale County take personal checks for recording?
faqs.a: No. Certified funds such as cashier's checks and money orders are accepted instead.

faqs.q: What hours does the Hillsdale County register keep?
faqs.a: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., in Room 212 at 33 McCollum St. Electronic filings can be sent any time but are processed in those hours.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a $175,000 Hillsdale County sale?
faqs.a: $1,505.00 in all: $1,312.50 to the state and $192.50 to the county, using 350 blocks of $500 at $4.30 each.
